summary: FireSync is a proposed web-based platform designed to bring NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspot observations together in a unified, accessible interface. The project aims to address the difficulty of comparing observations from different satellite sensors by organizing their data for geographical and historical analysis. Users will be able to explore fire hotspots through interactive maps, examine historical burning activity using calendars, and understand trends through data visualizations. Built around Python and Flask, FireSync aims to make satellite-derived fire information easier to explore and interpret for researchers, environmental organizations, students, and land managers. Our goal is to transform complex satellite observations into meaningful information that supports environmental monitoring and research.
details:
FireSync – Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS Active Fire Observations

What does your project do, and how does it work?

FireSync is a web-based platform that brings together active-fire observations from NASA FIRMS, using MODIS and VIIRS satellite data. It displays fire detections on an interactive map and presents details such as satellite source, acquisition time, location, confidence and Fire Radiative Power (FRP). Its harmonization feature compares observations from different sensors based on their geographical proximity and acquisition times, identifying potential cross-sensor matches.

What benefits does it have?

FireSync makes satellite fire data easier to explore and compare in one place. It helps users understand differences between satellite observations, identify nearby detections and examine fire activity without manually comparing separate datasets.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make satellite-based fire information more accessible and understandable, supporting researchers, students and other users exploring wildfire monitoring and Earth observation data.

What tools did you use?

Python, Flask, NASA FIRMS data services, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap.

How is your project creative?

FireSync combines observations from multiple satellite sensors in a single interactive environment. Instead of simply plotting detections, it introduces a spatial-and-temporal comparison approach that highlights potential matches and makes cross-sensor data exploration more intuitive. These matches are candidates for comparison, not confirmation that two observations represent the same physical fire.
